<details>
The provided `nyxuri-git.install` script contains only standard post-install and post-upgrade hook functions that print informational messages to the user. These messages guide the user on how to interact with the `nyxuri` application after installation or upgrade, such as running `nyxuri install full` or checking system health with `nyxuri doctor`. The script does not perform any file modifications, execute external downloads, spawn shells, or invoke dangerous commands.

All operations are limited to echoing help text and version management advice. References to paths like `/usr/share/nyxuri` and `~/.config` are descriptive and do not involve manipulation of those directories by the script itself. There is no use of `eval`, `curl`, `wget`, `base64`, or other high-risk constructs. The behavior aligns with standard AUR packaging practices for providing post-action guidance.

The script correctly adheres to the T1 contract mentioned, ensuring that user configuration state is not overwritten during upgrades, promoting user control over configuration reconciliation. This is a safe and expected pattern in AUR packages, especially for applications managing their own configuration lifecycle.
</details>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard Arch Linux package for `nyxuri-git`, a rolling-release desktop suite. It clones the source from a legitimate upstream GitHub repository (`https://github.com/ech678/Nyxuri.git`) using a VCS source URL, which is normal for `-git` packages. The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` entry is expected and acceptable for Git sources, as checksums are not applicable to mutable checkouts — this is standard AUR practice and not a red flag.

The build process consists of copying the project files (engine, unit blueprints, shell, catalog, and changelog) into the package directory under `/usr/share/nyxuri`, creating symlinks for the CLI and shell entry points in `/usr/bin`, installing license files, and cleaning up development-related files and bytecode caches. All operations are confined to the package build environment (`$srcdir`, `$pkgdir`) and follow standard packaging practices. There are no network operations during build time, no use of `eval`, `curl|bash`, or `wget`, and no obfuscated code.

Dependencies are auto-generated but clearly scoped: runtime dependencies are in `depends`, while optional components are listed in `optdepends` with descriptive comments. The `pkgver()` function uses `git describe` to generate version strings safely. No system modifications, backdoors, data exfiltration, or execution of fetched remote code occurs. The package behaves as expected for an AUR maintainer-provided build script.
</details>
